title: Migrate Rust panic-based parsers to Result<T, String>
description: The rust_num_parser library uses unwrap() everywhere. Migrate all three public functions to return Result<T, String> and add 3 error-path tests.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/lib.rs from panic-based to Result-based error handling.

New signatures:
  pub fn parse_int(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>
  pub fn parse_pair(s: &str) -> Result<(i32, i32), String>
  pub fn parse_and_sum(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>

Rules:
- Use map_err(|e| e.to_string()) to convert parse errors
- parse_pair must return Err if the string has no comma or either part fails to parse
- parse_and_sum delegates to parse_pair and propagates errors with ?
- Keep the 3 existing tests passing (update them to use .unwrap() on the Ok variant)
- Add 3 new error-path tests:
  - parse_int_invalid: parse_int('abc') is Err
  - parse_pair_no_comma: parse_pair('nope') is Err
  - parse_and_sum_invalid: parse_and_sum('1,x') is Err

Run cargo test to confirm all 6 tests pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
